commit: v0.6.5 (33b5d03e) plus the line-timing change of #382 (d8eb5dee), which touches src/main/asr/live-worker.ts and scripts/gates/g6-live-latency.ts only and logs nothing unless AKOU_LINE_TIMING=1
app: run from source with Bun (bun src/main/cli/cli.ts), headless; the release has no Windows app build
helpers: akou-capture 0.6.5 and akou-diarize 0.6.5, built on the box from the v0.6.5 sources with Rust 1.97.1 (cargo build --locked --release); sha256 b23afb7b95e8289e0fe202f867479261884f95fe077b73af5d1ce4a2d6cbb6e7 and a73454d8f412a991699dfd8eeeda5f8dac08d37419a7ec02a82fe8802b9b6baa
clips: scripts/gates/g6-clips.sh (macOS say, voice Samantha), the same 24 sentences and 56 s stereo timeline as the 2026-10-07 run
machine: a Windows x64 box (the machine of the 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-09 x64 runs), pinned to four performance cores with one thread each: processor affinity 0x55, set with cmd start /affinity 55 and read back from every akou process during each run
command: AKOU_HOME=<scratch> AKOU_HEADLESS=1 AKOU_CAPTURE_FILE_ONLY=1 AKOU_LINE_TIMING=1 bun scripts/gates/g6-live-latency.ts --cli src/main/cli/cli.ts --clips <48k> --wav <timeline.wav> --words <the 12 words> --out <file>

config.capture.helper: a wrapper that runs akou-capture with --from-wav <timeline> --realtime

conditions: one run at a time, alternating diarizers, each started only with no GitHub Actions runner process on the box and CPU load of 4 % or less; every run started a cold app
reading: In result.rows, latencyMs is the committed line (seg revision 1) minus the wall time the utterance's speech ended, and speakerMs is when the line first carried a speaker other than c?. decodeMs is the Worker's own time for the line's decode, provisionals and provisionalMs the re-decodes of its open segment before it, and behindMs how far behind the captured audio the Worker was when the decode started. result.clockSteps lists wall-clock steps of 50 ms or more that the gate script saw against the monotonic clock. cpu.samples has one row about every 1.2 s: wall and monotonic time, CPU of all 24 logical CPUs together, of each of the four pinned ones (0, 2, 4, 6) and of the busiest other one, then the CPU of processes by group, in percent of one logical CPU (400 is four full cores). The groups: akou (bun, akou-capture, akou-diarize and the wrapper), sampler (the PowerShell sampler and the WMI provider it queries, which run off the pinned cores), defender (Windows Defender), windows (other Windows services) and otherApps (every other program on the box, not named). cpuSecondsStartToEnd is the same grouping from the process list taken at the start and the end of the run. samplerClockStepMaxMs is the largest difference between wall and monotonic time across two samples. systemEvents is the Windows System event log inside the run.

rows.text: The ACA recorder keeps the microphone on the left channel.
Parakeet transcribes both sides of the call.
We moved the dashboards from Datadog to Grafana last week.
Silero decides where each segment starts and ends.
The Terraform Plan touched three Kubernetes clusters.
Please open a Zendesk ticket for the billing question.
TitaNet gives every speaker a voice print.
The final pass runs pianoed over the whole call.
ElectroBun hosts the window and the tray item.
Opus files stay playable while they are being written.
Can you share the Grafana link with the team?
Yes, the Kubernetes upgrade is scheduled for Friday.
I think Datadog was cheaper for us in the end.
Let us check what Akau heard in the last five minutes.
The Parakeet model runs on the CPU with two threads.
Zendesk and Terraform both need a new owner.
We should keep ElectroBun pinned until the next release.
Silero and TitaNet both run in the same worker.
Send me the Opus file after the call ends.
Who owns the Pianode configuration now?
The demo went well and the customer asked for pricing.
Thanks everyone. See you all next Tuesday.
Could you repeat the last number, please?
Okay, I will write the action items down.
